parameters.query:
-- Give back offers nobody answered. offered_appointment_id is deliberately KEPT: it is the
-- record that this person already had their chance at this slot, so the queue rolls forward
-- instead of looping back to them.
WITH reaped AS (
  UPDATE waitlist_entry SET status = 'waiting', offer_expires_at = NULL
  WHERE status = 'offered' AND (offer_expires_at IS NULL OR offer_expires_at < now())
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT json_build_object('reaped', (SELECT count(*) FROM reaped)) AS result;

-- One statement, because every part of it has to agree: pick a freed window, pick who is
-- next in line for it, write them the offer they can say yes to, and claim their place in the
-- queue — all or nothing.
--
-- The order matters. The customer's read-back is written FIRST and only if they are not in the
-- middle of something else; the queue claim then applies only to the people that actually
-- reached. Claiming first would hold a slot for half an hour for someone who was never told.
WITH freed AS (
  SELECT a.id, a.stylist_id, a.service_id, a.starts_at, a.ends_at, a.client_id AS cancelled_by
  FROM appointment a
  WHERE a.status = 'cancelled'
    -- Nobody wants a 30-minute window to accept a slot that starts in eight minutes.
    AND a.starts_at > now() + interval '60 minutes'
    -- Still genuinely free: an ordinary customer may have taken it already.
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM appointment b
                    WHERE b.stylist_id = a.stylist_id AND b.status = 'confirmed'
                      AND tstzrange(b.starts_at, b.ends_at) && tstzrange(a.starts_at, a.ends_at))
    -- One live offer per window: two people holding the same slot is the thing to avoid.
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM waitlist_entry w
                    WHERE w.offered_appointment_id = a.id AND w.status = 'offered')
), cand AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (f.id)
         f.id AS freed_id, f.stylist_id, f.starts_at, f.ends_at,
         w.id AS entry_id, w.client_id, c.name AS client_name, c.phone AS client_phone,
         c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id AS user_key,
         sv.id AS service_id, sv.name AS service_name, sv.duration_min, sv.price_php,
         st.name AS stylist_name
  FROM freed f
  JOIN waitlist_entry w ON w.status = 'waiting' AND w.service_id = f.service_id
       AND tstzrange(w.window_start, w.window_end) && tstzrange(f.starts_at, f.ends_at)
       AND w.offered_appointment_id IS DISTINCT FROM f.id         -- already had their chance
       AND w.client_id <> f.cancelled_by                          -- not their own cancelled slot
  JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = w.client_id
  JOIN service sv ON sv.id = w.service_id
  JOIN stylist st ON st.id = f.stylist_id
  -- The freed stylist has to actually do this service.
  JOIN stylist_service ss ON ss.stylist_id = f.stylist_id AND ss.service_id = w.service_id
  WHERE COALESCE(btrim(c.channel_user_id), '') <> ''              -- reachable
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM waitlist_entry w2                -- one outstanding offer per person:
                    WHERE w2.client_id = w.client_id AND w2.status = 'offered')
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM appointment ap                   -- and not already busy themselves
                    WHERE ap.client_id = w.client_id AND ap.status = 'confirmed'
                      AND tstzrange(ap.starts_at, ap.ends_at) && tstzrange(f.starts_at, f.ends_at))
  ORDER BY f.id, w.created_at, w.id                                -- deterministic queue order
), told AS (
  UPDATE bot_user_profile p
     SET pending_booking = json_build_object(
           'kind', 'book', 'waitlist_entry_id', cand.entry_id,
           'booking_key', 'wl:' || cand.entry_id || ':' || extract(epoch from now())::bigint,
           'service_id', cand.service_id, 'service_name', cand.service_name,
           'duration_min', cand.duration_min, 'price_php', cand.price_php,
           'stylist_id', cand.stylist_id, 'stylist_name', cand.stylist_name, 'stylist_requested', false,
           'date', to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'YYYY-MM-DD'),
           'time', to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'HH24:MI'),
           'starts_at_utc',   to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
           'starts_at_local', to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'),
           'weekday', to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Day'),
           'client_name', cand.client_name, 'client_phone', cand.client_phone,
           'summary', cand.service_name || ' with ' || cand.stylist_name || ' on '
                      || to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon HH24:MI'))::jsonb,
         pending_set_at = now(), updated_at = now()
    FROM cand
   WHERE p.user_key = cand.user_key
     -- Never talk over a live conversation: if they are mid-booking with the agent, their
     -- read-back stands and this slot waits for the next run.
     AND (p.pending_booking IS NULL OR p.pending_set_at < now() - interval '30 minutes')
  RETURNING p.user_key, cand.entry_id, cand.freed_id
), claimed AS (
  UPDATE waitlist_entry w
     SET status = 'offered', offered_appointment_id = told.freed_id,
         offer_expires_at = now() + interval '30 minutes'
    FROM told
   WHERE w.id = told.entry_id AND w.status = 'waiting'
  RETURNING w.id AS entry_id, told.freed_id
)
SELECT c.entry_id, c.freed_id AS appointment_id, 'client' AS recipient, 'offer' AS kind,
       format('Good news %s — a %s with %s opened up on %s. It is yours if you reply yes in the next 30 minutes.',
              cand.client_name, cand.service_name, cand.stylist_name,
              to_char(cand.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon, HH24:MI')) AS text,
       c.entry_id AS waitlist_entry_id
FROM claimed c JOIN cand ON cand.entry_id = c.entry_id;

parameters.content:
## 31 · filling a cancellation

A slot falls through; somebody on the waitlist gets it.

The offer is written as the customer's **pending read-back** — exactly what the agent writes when it reads a booking back — so their "yes" runs the ordinary booking path and the EXCLUDE constraint decides who actually gets it. No special acceptance route, no second way to create an appointment.

One person is offered at a time, in `created_at` order. An offer expires after 30 minutes and rolls to the next — and because the entry remembers which appointment it was offered, it never loops back to someone who already passed.

It will not talk over a live conversation: a customer mid-booking keeps their own read-back and the slot waits for the next run.
